name: 'Povera' Shed Exhibition
description:
'Povera' meaning 'poor art' in Italian, is an ongoing project made by mixed-media artist Michael Connell. 

In his back garden in Catford, Michael has built an unbelievable shed, fusing art and nature, that's made entirely of waste materials from skips and people's unwanted items.

Exploring themes of music, family, heritage and nature, step inside the ever-evolving magic of the Povera shed.

name: 1 Pontypool Place
description: Tour of home & garden designed in 2018 by Nagan Johnson Architects
address: 1 Pontypool Place London London, Greater London, SE1 8QF

name: 12 Church Grove
description: The first residents have moved into the capital’s biggest community-led self-build project, coordinated by the Rural Urban Synthesis Society (RUSS): 36 flats in two linked buildings, a new public riverside garden and shared community spaces. As a Community Land Trust, RUSS aims to create sustainable and permanently affordable homes in a community woven into the wider communities of Lewisham.

name: 141 Coldershaw Road, W13
description: The home of Eric and Jessica Huntley , community activists and educators who founded the pioneering company Bogle-L'Ouverture Publications in 1968, lived and ran their bookshop from this semi detached property soon after.  The house is a Black British cultural archivists dream; filled with books, arts and craft and correspondence from the 1960s to the present day.

name: 18 Lauradale Road
description:
Fantastic views across an archery field to Highgate Woods are the focus of two new contemporary extensions to a small family house in Muswell Hill.
Features include: Green roof, Zinc cladding, Stainless steel kitchen, Beautiful tiling, Big windows, Pebbledash crown, and a sculptural concrete bench.

name: 2 Belgrave Road: Victorian house with Luis Barragán inspired interior
description:
A Luis Barragán inspired design for the interior of a typical late Victorian house in East London. 
The use of bold vivid colour banishes the sterility that can accompany modernism without the loss of its hallmark simplicity and elegant line. This approach can be accommodated within houses whose external architecture has a very different heritage. Its achievement does not require a big budget

name: 25 Brunswick Street
description: Full refurbishment and extension of a Victorian terraced house in Walthamstow Village. The project reconfigures a previously compromised layout to create a brighter, more coherent home, improving its relationship to the street and garden. A careful material palette and environmental upgrades enhance both spatial quality and long-term performance.

name: 44 Monsell Road
description: 44 is a reconfiguration and extension of a charming and peculiar Victorian house. The original building was an opportunistic infill in the garden of an adjacent home, sitting alone behind two terraced streets. The architect and home owner saw the potential to expand the modest building, creating a pocket home which keeps their growing family in the community they have called home for 15 years.

name: 6 Fitzroy Square, The Georgian Group
description: As part of Vanbrugh300, step inside the Georgian Group's historic headquarters at 6 Fitzroy Square for a day of talks, exhibitions and rare access celebrating the life and legacy of Sir John Vanbrugh.
address: The Georgian Group, 6 Fitzroy Square, W1T 5DX

name: 6 Moretown (Gensler London Studio)
description: A contemporary adaptation of a 1980s office building, and home of global design firm Gensler. Each level of the building is connected by a structural timber facade and set of stairs, and the new 5th floor cantilevers from the roof.

name: A IS FOR ARCHITECTURE - 493 Hackney Road
description: While cafes, markets, and restaurants come and go, the high street once felt immutable until online shopping and same-day delivery eroded its vitality. Our office at 493 Hackney Rd, once London’s oldest ironmongers, then a plant shop, was renovated to preserve character and serve as our long term base. We look forward to continuing the journey of opening our shop to new visitors and collaborators.

name: A Ruskinian Walk Through Shared Heritage
description: Ruskinian walk from RIBA award-winning Chiswick Business Park, Gunnersbury Triangle Nature Reserve through South Acton Estate, birthplace of artist Patrick Caulfield; Woodlands Park Ice House; to home of William Willett, initiator of Daylight Saving Time.
address: Building 3, Chiswick Business Park, 566 Chiswick High Road, W4 5YA

name: ACAVA Blechynden Street Studios
description: Blechynden Street Studios is a purpose-built artist studio complex in London, completed in 1999. It was the first of its kind in the city for decades and remains one of the few dedicated studio buildings in London. The distinctive deck-style architecture features walkways leading to 21 individual studios, each with floor-to-ceiling double-glazed windows that provide natural light.

name: ACAVA Camden Undercraft Studios
description:
ACAVA Undercraft Studios
A vital creative hub in Gospel Oak, home to 34 fully accessible artist studios and 10 community organisations.
address: Blue Double Door, 48-72 Ludham, Lismore Circus,, NW5 4SF

name: Aga Khan Centre
description: The Aga Khan Centre, designed by Pritzker prize winning architect Fumihiko Maki, houses the UK institutions of the Aga Khan Development Network. A unique feature is its six gardens inspired by different regions of the Muslim world.
address: Aga Khan Centre, 10 Handyside Street, N1C 4DN

name: Alexandra Palace: Mindful walking and drawing tour
description: Join local artist Emily Wood Ahmed for a mindful walking and drawing tour around  the grounds of Alexandra Palace in Haringey, North London. Through gentle walking, mindful drawing and local stories, you will discover the artists of 'Ally Pally', past and present, create your own artwork, enjoy one of London’s most spectacular panoramic views, and finish at Birch Arts Gallery in Wood Green.
address: Alexandra Palace, Alexandra Palace Way, N22 7AY

name: All's well in Camberwell: walking London's local government history
description: This walking tour explores the evolution of local government through the story of Camberwell. It charts the development of institutions in response to intense social and economic change to shape the city we know today. We will celebrate the visible reminders of this history in the streets around us and ask: why does this matter to Londoners today?

name: Allies and Morrison Open Studio
description: Allies and Morrison opens its studios, offering a chance to see inside of one of the UK's largest architecture and urbanism practices. Two buildings - one concrete, one timber - have been designed and adapted by Allies and Morrison to create the compact, integrated campus of studio space that the practice calls home. Guided tours will include the workplaces, terraces and modelshop.

name: Architectural Walk in Brockley
description: Brockley Conservation Area's High Victorian enclave holds many interesting houses in a variety of styles, including Edwardian domestic architecture, historic trees and original lanes and mews. These have survived into the 21st century almost intact. Houses built in the 1950s and 1960s indicate WWII bomb damage and add to the area's variety and history.

name: Art and architecture in Thamesmead
description: On the surface Thamesmead might seem concrete and grey, but on this tour we will take a look at the colour and life local artists are breathing into the area. Examining the past and present, we'll explore the abbey ruins, exciting sculptures, concrete skywalks, and vivid murals that make this place the Town of Tomorrow.
address: Outside the upper concourse of Abbey Wood Station, 513 Abbey Wood Rd

name: Art in Perpetuity Trust
description: Open Studios, provides a unique glimpse to the architectural spaces and working studios of APT artists.  Over the weekend, there is also the opportunity to see our Group Show in the Gallery, curated by and featuring APT artists' work.

name: Arts Network
description: We are an arts and mental health charity with a 30 year legacy in Lewisham, reframing mental health through creativity and community. We will be opening our studios and community garden in Deptford to the public and offering a free creative workshop.
address: Arts Network, Art Hub Studios, Mornington Centre, Stanley St, SE8 4BL

name: BBC Broadcasting House
description:
First ever purpose-built broadcast centre in UK, and a jewel of Art Deco design with original artworks by sculptor Eric Gill. 
Remodelled and extended in 2006/2013 by architects MacCormac Jamieson and Prichard/Sheppard Robson.

name: BT Tower
description: An enduring, distinctive feature of the London skyline for the last 54 years, this is a rare opportunity for members of the public to visit the famous revolving floor, 158m above the capital. After the flight the guests can watch a history of the BT Tower film in our auditorium.

name: Backstage at The Old Vic
description: Backstage at The Old Vic is a new build six-storey extension to the Grade II* listed Old Vic Theatre and marks a bold new chapter in the theatre’s remarkable 200-year story. Spaces include a triple-height Cafe/Bar, Script Library, Writers’ Room, Clore Learning Centre, flexible 90-seat Studio, Event Space with a roof terrace with views across the London skyline.

name: Baitul Futuh Mosque
description: Guided tours of the largest purpose-built mosque in Western Europe accommodating 14,000 worshippers blending of Islamic and modern British architecture. Recent developments, involving reconstruction after a fire were completed and the magnificent new complex was opened on 4th March 2023.
address: Ahmadiyya Muslim Association, 181 London Road, Morden, SM4 5PT

name: Bank of England Museum
description: The museum is part of the Bank of England rebuilding in the 1930's by Sir Herbert Baker. One room is a reconstruction of 1793 Bank of England Stock Office by Sir John Soane.

name: Beck Road Studios: Artist Open Studios & Exhibitions
description: Visit Beck Road Studios for an artist open studios event and a chance to explore 10 hidden studios in a railway arch. Meet the artists in person and discover their work, including painters, sculptors, photographer, fashion designer, furniture restorers, as well as an ethical vintage clothing label.

name: Bermondsey to Borough: hidden arches food walk
description: A lively food-history walk from Bermondsey to Borough, tracing how railway arches, markets, hop trading, coaching inns and migration have shaped how London eats. We will explore Spa Terminus, Maltby Street, The Hop Exchange, The George Inn and Borough’s market edge through stories of trade, travel, street food, preservation, neighbourhood change and hidden corners, past and present along the route.

name: Billingsgate Roman House & Baths
description: Some of London's best Roman remains, comprising late 2C house with a 3C bath house built within its courtyard. First discovered in 1848.

name: Birds Portchmouth Russum Architects  - Open Office
description: The office is an extraordinary gallery of sublime hand drawings and exquisite models of uniquely joyous architectural projects developed over 35 years that have been exhibited regularly at the Royal Academy Summer Show and in exhibitions around the world. Drop in and the founding directors will be on hand to explain and discuss the wonderful exhibits.
address: Unit 11 , Union Wharf., 23 Wenlock Road, N1 7SB

name: Blackheath Quaker Meeting House
description:
"A brutalist jewel", the meeting house was designed by Trevor Dannatt, who worked on the Royal Festival Hall.  
A 1970s concrete building with a raised lantern, it was designed to fit in with older buildings in the conservation area and to make the most of its split-level site. 
Grade ll Listed for its original design, it is used for Quaker worship and by community groups.

name: Blackhorse Workshop
description: A makerspace offering open access to a fully equipped wood and metal workshop with bench space, tools and machinery. Includes an education space, community café, and studios for creative businesses and artists.
address: Blackhorse Workshop, 1-2 Sutherland Road Path, E17 6BX

name: Blythe Hill House
description: Discover Blythe Hill House, a bold retrofit of a 1970s end-of-terrace home by Whittaker Parsons and Price & Myers. A striking courtyard extension transforms the house into a light-filled, fully electric family home, showcasing how ambitious architecture, low-carbon design and affordability can come together in suburban southeast London.

name: Bodney Road Studios
description: Bodney Road Studio's is home to a range of practitioners working in the built environment including architectural photographer Lorenzo Zandri, graphic designers Polytechnic and place futurists The Place Bureau. Join us on 19–20 September when we will open the studios in conjunction with a programme of exhibitions and events by Lorenzo Zandri, Polytechnic, Sammi Gale and The Place Bureau.

name: Boston Manor House
description: Boston Manor House is a Jacobean House built for Lady Mary Reade in 1623 and later owned by the Clitherow family from the 1670s until the 1920s. The House is now open to the public with free entry six days a week. Its beautifully restored historic interiors, including breath-taking ornate plasterwork, are joined by two community exhibition galleries, meeting rooms and an attractive modern café.
address: Boston Manor House, Boston Manor Road, Brentford, TW8 9JX

name: Bower House
description: Grade I listed country house commanding the most extensive southerly views over Essex. Staircase mural by Sir James Thornhill, a painter notable for the 'Painted Hall' at the Royal Naval Hospital at Greenwich. Set in grounds with a pond.
address: Orange Tree Hill, Havering-atte-Bower, Romford, RM4 1PB

name: Brentham Garden Suburb
description: Britain's first co-partnership garden suburb, first houses built in 1901. Parker and Unwin's plan introduced in 1907, mainly Arts and Crafts style; fascinating social history.
address: The Brentham Club, 38 Meadvale Road, W5 1NP

name: Brick Sixty Studio
description:
A rare chance to see behind the scenes at the newly located Brick Sixty Studio on Roman Road, London.

This stock brick Victorian shop with accommodation above, was refurbished this year by Architectural Workshop. Now home to Brick Sixty, who design and make products in the form of the much-loved London brick and are looking to support local makers & craft in the UK with the new space.
address: Brick Sixty, 469 Roman Rd, E3 5LX, E3 5LX

name: Broadway Theatre
description:
Built in 1932 by architects Bradshaw Gass & Hope .
This iconic Grade II listed venue is a unique blend of architectural elements including Art Deco, Tudor and Gothic Revival.  
The theatre was planned by Lewisham Metropolitan Council in the 1920s, to be an auditorium for “a variety of Civic, Social and Dramatic purposes”.  
It is a much loved community asset, join us for a full tour.
address: Broadway Theatre, Rushey Green, Catford, SE6 4RU

name: Bromley and Sheppard's College
description: Founded to house the widows of clergymen, the original building consisted of 20 houses built around a classically-styled quadrangle. Captain Richard Ryder – one of Sir Christopher Wren's surveyors – was in charge of design and construction.
address: London Road (entrance via Wren Gates, no vehicle entry), Bromley

name: Bullers Wood School for Girls
description:
Typical mid-Victorian stucco-fronted house built on a grassy hillside, extended in 1888 by Ernest Newton with William Morris redesigning the interiors. The library, formerly drawing room, has a unique William Morris hand-painted ceiling.
The school itself has a range of older and newer buildings, including Inglewood House. The grounds will be open during the Open House festival.

name: Burlington House: Linnean Society of London
description: The world's oldest active biological society. Founded in 1788, the Society takes its name from the Swedish naturalist Carl Linnaeus whose botanical, zoological and library collections have been in its keeping since 1829.

name: Burlington House: Royal Astronomical Society
description: The Royal Astronomical Society (RAS) moved into Burlington House in 1874. Part of the extension to Burlington House, to provide accommodation for learned societies, the building was refurbished in 2007. The RAS is the oldest astronomical society in the world and has been encouraging and promoting the study of astronomy and geophysics since 1820.

name: Burlington House: Royal Society of Chemistry
description:
Experience the history, architecture and science of the east wing of Burlington House that's been home to the Royal Society of Chemistry (formerly The Chemical Society) since 1967.

The east and west wings, along with the facade along Piccadilly were built in 1873 as an addition to the existing house that was originally built in 1664.

name: Burlington House: The Geological Society of London
description: Home to the oldest geological society in the world, founded in 1807. The Society has been based at Burlington House since 1874, and now has over 12,000 members worldwide.

name: Carpenters' Hall
description: Livery Hall first built in 1429, much altered then demolished and rebuilt in 1880, destroyed in 1941 except for external walls (W W Pocock). Designed as a showpiece for the craft of carpentry, the third Hall on the site.

name: Castlands Road
description: Set on a quiet Victorian terraced street in Catford, Castlands Road is a personal work of architecture. A small site street infill designed and self-built by Will and Sogand Howard as a low-energy home for their young family, the project transforms a rear garden into a prototypical three-bedroom house, built with limited means and careful attention to how skills and resources are drawn upon.

name: Cecil Sharp House
description: Purpose built to house the English Folk Dance and Song Society, this Grade II listed building was designed by members of the Art Workers Guild of the time. Bomb damaged in 1940, rebuilt and reopened in 1950. Iconic Ivon Hitchins mural.

name: Charing Cross Library
description: The building has had many incarnations since its construction in the 1890s as a woolen warehouse.   It became a home to the Italian Benevolent Society, then a fascist club, a serviceman's club, and now a library with the largest publicly accessible collection of Chinese language books in the UK.  View the temporary exhibition on the Matteotti Affair.

name: Christ Church Southgate and the Minchenden Oak Garden
description: Grade II* listed church with fine collection of Pre-Raphaelite stained glass windows by Morris & Co. including Burne Jones and Rossetti. Wall paintings. Mosaic reredos of the Last Supper by Antonio Salviati. Minchenden Oak  - ancient pollarded oak more than 800 years old.

name: Christ Lutheran Church, Petts Wood
description: A small but perfectly-formed expression of late modernist ecclesiastical architecture deep within the south-eastern suburbs of London, only rarely open to the public for purposes other than religious services.

name: Christ's Chapel of God's Gift at Dulwich
description: Christ’s Chapel in Dulwich, consecrated in 1616, is an active place of worship and Grade II-listed chapel in the heart of Dulwich Village. It was conceived as the focus for the College of God's Gift, founded by the Elizabethan actor-manager and entrepreneur Edward Alleyn (1566-1626), a complex which also comprised of a school and almshouses and which still provides homes to older residents.

name: Church of St Andrew the Apostle
description: St Andrew's is a Grade II* listed building by Philip Appleby Robson (1871–1951). It boasts a magnificent Arts and Crafts interior with rich wood carvings in the chancel and magnificent stained-glass windows by the renowned Martin Travers (1886–1948) and Lawrence Stanley Lee (1909–2011), who also has work in Coventry Cathedral.

name: City Information Centre
description: London's main tourist information centre is clad in a specially manufactured system of 220 pre-finished stainless steel panels. The subtly reflective surface provides a striking counterpoint to St Paul's.

name: Cody Dock - Lea Way Celebration
description: Our event will focus on celebrating the rich heritage of Cody Dock, one of the last remaining brick-lined docks in London.  Our one-day festival will provide exciting opportunities to explore the lesser-known history of the Lower Lea Valley

name: Coopers' Hall
description: Coopers' Hall is a late 17th century, timber-framed merchant's house with a Georgian frontage. A Livery Hall since 1957, it features a fine Courtoom, dining room and an impressive staircase spiralling up the entire height of the building. The building displays artefacts of the coopers' trade (the making of wooden casks such as barrels) and is the home of the Worshipful Company of Coopers

name: Corbett Community Library
description: Visit the Grade II listed Corbett Community Library building. This beautifully preserved Edwardian building is rich in architectural character and heritage, featuring , an impressive dome, ornate door handles, some stained glass and a historic brass plaque. Discover the history and craftsmanship of this remarkable community landmark during your visit.
address: Corbett Community Library, 103 Torridon Road, SE6 1RQ

name: County Hall Kingston
description:
London Square presents a rare opportunity to step inside a sensitively restored former Surrey County Hall, which will be transformed into a collection of contemporary new-build homes to buy and commercial areas for hire.

Set in the heart of Kingston, this is a unique opportunity to experience County Hall from the inside out—before its next chapter begins.

name: Crown Court Church of Scotland
description: A Church of Scotland in London, home to the longest-established Presbyterian congregation in London, worshipping in this location in Covent Garden since 1719. The current building is red brick with Portland stone dressings in a restrained, finely crafted Free Style. Three storeys, recessed slated attic, mullioned and transomed windows. Fine stained glass, most of which is by Farrar Bell.

name: Croydon Town Hall
description: Croydon Town Hall will be opened for a limited number of guided tours, providing rare access to this unique Victorian-style, Grade II listed building. Croydon Town Hall was designed by local architect Charles Henman and opened in 1896.

name: Croydon Urban Room
description:
The Croydon Urban Room is a space to talk about the past, present and future of the Croydon town centre. Through conversa­tions, stories, exhibitions and events, the Urban Room brings together the views of those who live, work and visit the area to create a shared vision of the future and test new uses live in action. 

See our website for further details of specific events.

name: Crystal Palace Park Dinosaurs  – a tour with a London Blue Badge Tourist Guide
description:
Explore the world's first dinosaur models hidden in a south London park. The 30 Grade I listed, life-size statues of dinosaurs and other extinct animals at Crystal Palace Park have thrilled
visitors for 166 years. Tour is kids friendly.
address: Crystal Palace Overground station, Crystal Palace Overground station

name: Cultivating Community - LightHouse Gardens & IQL North
description: Discover a magical garden hidden behind hoarding in Stratford! The LightHouse & Gardens is a meanwhile space run by locals, featuring Community Sauna CIC. Rooted in human connection, it acts as an incubator for the area. Join Hadley Property Group for a site tour, view a model and explore future plans for the site through Augmented Reality.

name: Culture House
description: Culture House is the first permanent exhibition space for Somali artefacts curated by the Somali community.

name: Cumberland Road Studios, Wood Green
description:
The Cumberland Road Studios Wood Green is host to about 50 artists and makers currently occupying studios in a 1980s former office building. You will have the opportunity to chat, and see their work and their workspaces as part of their Open Studios weekend.
The building will be active with events including workshops, demonstrations and talks.

name: Dalston Eastern Curve Garden
description: A vital community garden offering a model for maximum good for communities and for the environment on a small urban plot. It is now recognised as a site of Local Importance for Nature Conservation. Winner of an Open City Stewardship Award 2021.

name: David Lean Cinema Tour
description: Croydon Council's ambitious 1990s Croydon Clocktower project created a large new central library. Former Town Hall library and other spaces were then repurposed as arts venues which opened in 1995. These tours will outline how this was achieved, with particular emphasis on the David Lean Cinema, and will include a brief talk on the cinema's eventful history.
address: Croydon Clocktower, Katharine Street, Croydon, CR9 1ET

name: Dr Johnson's House
description: Fine example of an early 5-floor Queen Anne town house with original panelling, open staircase and unique 'swinging panels' on the open-plan first floor. Johnson compiled his famous 'Dictionary of the English Language' (1755)  here.

name: Drawing Matter
description: Drawing Matter explores the role of drawing in architectural thought and practice. Central to our activities is the Drawing Matter Collection of many thousands of architectural and design drawings from across the world, dating from the Renaissance to the present day.

name: Easi-house
description: A reimagined Victorian terrace house full of light, joy and unexpected material flourishes. The project navigated challenging construction cost changes and changing personal circumstances for the whole team to make it happen. It is ultimately a reflection of a shared design vision but also the household’s own creativity and resourcefulness.

name: East End Farm Cottage
description: Three-bay timber-framed yeoman house built c1420 with list of previous owners dating back to 1429. Part wall painting of hunting scene on dining room wall (16C). Tudor upstairs window and a smoke room still intact. Entrance porch dates from 16C.

name: Eastbury Manor House
description: One of the finest surviving Elizabethan red brick Manor houses- Grade I listed. Contains 17th Century wall-paintings, charming walled garden and a fine Tudor tower with original stairs. Many original features have been restored and layout remains mostly unchanged in over 400 years.
address: Eastbury Manor House, Eastbury Square, Barking, IG11 9SN

name: Embassy of the Republic of Poland
description:
Georgian townhouse designed by the Adam Brothers in 1777-1778 and a fine example of Neoclassical interior design. It houses a collection of European artworks and includes a unique Edwardian Anglo-Japanese drawing room.  

Individual pre-booking is essential, a photo ID will be required upon entry. Airport-style security checks will also be in place, so please do not bring any heavy luggage.

name: English National Ballet
description: English National Ballet bring world-class dance to the widest possible audience, and invite you into their home, the Mulryan Centre for Dance. Book a free tour to go behind the scenes, attend a Rehearsal Insight Session, see professional dancers take class and get up close to some beautiful ballet costumes created by our wardrobe department.
address: English National Ballet, 41 Hopewell Square, E14 0SY

name: Fairfield Halls
description: Step inside Fairfield Halls for Open House Festival and explore one of Croydon’s most iconic buildings. Discover its history, uncover what happens behind the scenes, learn how productions and events are delivered across the venue, enjoy guided tours, and take part in activities throughout the day.

name: Farmers and Fletchers' Hall
description: Farmers and Fletchers' Hall is one of the 44 Livery Halls in the City of London.  The Hall is the home to both the Worshipful Company of Fletchers, an ancient Livery Company and the Farmers, a modern Livery Company.  The  Worshipful Company of Fletchers will open it's doors to show members of the public some of the modern work of the Fletchers Livery, it's traditions and heritage.

name: Flavours of Royal Docks: Food, Architecture & Memory
description: Discover the Royal Docks through food, architecture and shared memory. This walking tour explores how docks, mills, warehouses and factories shaped East London’s food system and the communities around them. Through sensory prompts, oral history conversations and storytelling, participants are invited to experience the built environment as a living archive of trade, migration and everyday life.
address: London City Hall, Kamal Chunchie Way, E16 1ZE

name: Fleet Street Heritage Wall and Sundial
description: The Fleet Street Heritage Wall comprises 86 A3 information panels about the people, places, ideas and newspapers which made the name of Fleet Street famous throughout the world.  From 17th to 20th Sept frequent talks will be given on the sundial and the Heritage Wall, and its innovative design features which will  make it accessible to all comers through web pages, Easy Read pages, and audio files

name: Forgotten stories at Ally Pally: Empire, Commonwealth and hidden histories
description: Beyond Alexandra Palace's iconic skyline lies a collection of remarkable stories that are often overlooked.  Join Linda Gyamfi, a Heritage Champion for Bruce Castle Museum & Archive and a member of the Golden Key Academy, for a journey into the forgotten stories of Alexandra Palace. We will uncover Alexandra Palace's connections to Britain's imperial past.
address: Alexandra Palace, Alexandra Palace Way, Wood Green, N22 7AY

name: Former Carbonic Gas Works, 142 Lea Bridge Road
description:
Paradise works artist studios in the Old Carbonic Works that is thought to be the birthplace of commercial fizzy drinks in the late 18th Century. It features in the Lea Valley and Hackney Conservation area report found online.


https://hackney.moderngov.co.uk/documents/s68747/240220%20Appendix%20A%20Lea%20Bridge%20Conservation%20Area%20Appraisal.pdf
address: Paradise works, 142 Lea Bridge Road, E5 9RB

name: Founders' Hall
description: Founders’ Hall is the home of the Worshipful Company of Founders (one of the City’s ancient livery companies). Built in the 1980s with a striking and eclectic design, the Hall preserves historic traits whilst embracing modern ideas. Drop in during Open House to explore its treasures, meet members, and enjoy activities for all ages!

name: Four Corners
description: Refurbished extended building, a centre for film and photography. Central courtyard integrated 'hub' allows light and air to filter through. Loft conversion to create studio and work space. Sustainable features include sedum roof.

name: Free Clothes Mending Make Mee Studio
description:
Have the moths made a meal of your favourite jumper? Are your jeans coming undone at the seams?

Join Make Mee Studio and Lewisham Council to learn how to prolong the life of your clothes and homewares, whether it's darning a sock or patching a cushion cover we can show you how to mend and repair and bring it back to life.
address: Crofton Park Community Library, 375 Brockley Road, SE4 2AG

name: From Elephant to Peckham
description: This tour explores the architectural and social histories of Elephant & Castle, Walworth and Peckham through successive waves of regeneration. The tour draws on research into South London gentrification – examining Victorian and Brutalist housing, town planning, transport, heritage and community change, and tracing the area's evolution from rural Surrey settlements to contemporary redevelopment.
address: Entrance to Elephant & Castle station, Elephant Rd, SE17 1GD

name: From Forest to Morris: A walk around Walthamstow
description: A walk around historic Walthamstow showing how this unique area grew from a village into a thriving suburb, its social history and the variety of buildings that can be found where Epping Forest meets William Morris.
address: Outside Costa Coffee at Walthamstow Central Station 5 Station Approac

name: Fruit to Fashion: how a kitchen garden became a world famous piazza
description:
This year marks the 52nd  anniversary of when the wholesale market ceased trading and moved to the Battersea/Vauxhall area . The tour charts the evolution of Covent Garden, incorporating the piazza, the wholesale produce market, social residential areas and supporting neighbourhoods, and highlighting the social and commercial highs, lows and challenges.
Contact tonyganio@gmail.com

name: Garage Gallery E17
description: In 2022 we created an art gallery in the garage below our house in a residential street in Walthamstow village.   We aim to bring art into our community, acting as a resource to support artists on a not-for-profit basis.  By the time of Open House we will have hosted 26 exhibitions in a wide range of media, by both emerging and more experienced artists.

name: Georgian Clerkenwell's speculative housing boom
description: The early 1800's saw the green fields of northern Clerkenwell spring up into grand squares and terraced houses. This walking tour will look at how the speculative housing developed, what remains today, and the unique stories and characters of the area.
address: Outside Sadler's Wells Theatre, Rosebery Avenue, EC1R 4TN

name: Georgian Grafton Street: Sprüth Magers Gallery
description: Join SAVE Britain's Heritage and Klaud Studio for a tour of Sprüth Magers gallery in Mayfair, a sensitively restored Grade II-listed townhouse by Sir Robert Taylor. Discover how its layered history was honoured and past damage repaired to create a refined, modern space for art, clients, and work.

name: Glenkerry House
description: Glenkerry House is a 14-storey tower block designed by Hungarian architect Ernő Goldfinger. The block is managed by its residents, who collectively form the Glenkerry Co-operative Housing Association.

name: Gongoozlers of Regent's Canal & Victoria Park
description: Calling all canal enthusiasts - known as gongoozlers - to walk through the social and industrial history of Victoria Park, Haggerston, and Islington along Regent's Canal. Discover how a purpose-built canal shaped the lives of East Enders, Londoners, and the United Kingdom.
address: Bonner Gate, Sewardstone Road, Bethnal Green, E2 9JW

name: Gothic Lodge Garden
description: We're opening our Garden for tours of our outdoor spaces.  These spaces are maintained by adults with learning disabilities who attend our day activities programme, We'll also share a little of the history and significance of Gothic Lodge, a building housed within our garden and one of London's earliest concrete Houses.  Note: we will only view the exterior of the building.
address: L'Arche Garden Workshop, 2 Barston Road, SE27 9HE

name: Grand Junction at St Mary Magdalene Church, Paddington
description: Grade I Victorian Gothic church by G E Street, architect of the Royal Courts of Justice. The recent conservation project reveals the majestic colours of Daniel Bell's painted ceiling, plus Dow Jones Architects' contemporary heritage wing.
address: Rowington Close, St Mary Magdalene's Church, W2 5TF

name: Green Lodge
description: Green Lodge is a low-energy family home by Stylus Architects, carefully embedded into the landscape of Putney Heath. Much of the accommodation is concealed below ground, allowing the building to maintain a modest presence whilst bringing natural light into every room through a series of lightwells and rooflights.

name: Greenwich Yacht Club
description: Greenwich Yacht Club is an iconic riverside clubhouse with panoramic views of the Thames, the O2 and the Thames Barrier. Completed in 2000, it has served a club founded in 1908. Activities include dinghy sailing, cruising, rowing, racing and RYA classes. Facilities include a sail loft, machine shop, construction shed and a landside building for weddings and other events.

name: Guided Tours and Exhibition at Pioneer Centre, Peckham
description:
Grade II* Listed Modernist building, famously described by Walter Gropius as "an oasis of glass in a desert of brick". Originally built to house 'The Peckham Experiment' an innovative health centre in the 1930s. It was converted to private dwellings in 2000, retaining the indoor pool. 

Join members of our new Community Interest Company set up to mark the centenary and share this unique story.

name: Guildhall
description: The City's seat of municipal government since 12C. Grade I listed, rare example of medieval civic architecture. Historic banqueting hall and a site of major moments in British history that is still used today.

name: Guildhall Art Gallery
description:
Open daily 10am-5pm. 
Regular free guided tours 12.15pm & 1.15pm on Tuesday-Sunday, with extra tours on the final Open House weekend.
Home of the City of London's art collection, & remains of London's Roman Amphitheatre

name: Guildhall Library
description: Purpose built over 5 floors to house printed books and manuscripts. Features include former pneumatic tube ticket delivery system and 56 listed translucent pyramid roof lights.

name: Haberdashers' Hall
description: Designed by Sir Michael Hopkins and Partners, Haberdashers' Hall reinterprets the traditional livery hall for the 21st century: a cloistered courtyard bordered by a brick loggia and lead-panelled roof. It is the Haberdashers' Company's fourth hall, and was opened by Her Majesty the Queen in 2002.
address: 18 West Smithfield (opposite Barts Hospital by traffic barrier under

name: Hackney Empire
description: Hackney Empire is a grade II* listed building. The theatre was built as a music hall in 1901, designed by the architect Frank Matcham. It is now a variety theatre for the 21st century, serving the local community and beyond.

name: Hammersmith Quaker Meeting House
description: Recently designated as a Building of Cultural Interest by the Council, the Quaker Meeting House is designed to be a highly sustainable building to embody the Quaker values of simplicity and equality.  The award winning building promotes a sense of calm and tranquility.

name: Hampstead Heath Pergola
description: 800ft long Grade II* listed pergola is designed in one of London's secret gardens at the rear of Inverforth House, Lord Leverhulme's London residence (1904-25).
address: Inverforth Close (off North End Way), NW3 7EX

name: Hermitage Community Moorings
description: A development of residential and recreational moorings for historic vessels on the Thames. The unique Pier House, built to a high specification, provides a floating community centre just downstream from Tower Bridge.

name: Herne Hill Velodrome
description:
Herne Hill Velodrome, opened in 1891, hosted track cycling events for the 1948 Olympics, is now home to a thriving grassroots cycling facility - hosting everything from Learn to Cycle to local and international racing events. 
HHV overcame the threat of closure in the early 2000s, and a new pavilion, designed by Mike Taylor of Hopkins Architects, opened in 2017.

name: Highgate School Chapel, Library, Museum
description: Founded by Sir Roger Cholmeley, Lord Chief Justice of England, in 1565, Highgate School is governed as a single charitable foundation. Highgate School combines Victorian buildings (our Chapel, Central Hall classrooms and Sir Martin Gilbert Library) with modern facilities.

name: Highpoint
description: Grade I listed Modernist apartment blocks retaining many original features.

name: Historic & Modern Buildings in the City
description: On this walk, we will see many historic & modern buildings in the City of London. We’ll look at different architecture styles having regard to the environment and sustainability, from heritage sites to pioneering green tech. Hear about famous architects, past and present, as we explore how the Square Mile preserves its legacy while evolving for a resilient, carbon-neutral tomorrow.

name: Hogarth's House
description: Early 18th century red brick country home of artist William Hogarth, extended significantly c. 1749-1764. The 2020 extension, funded by the National Lottery Heritage Fund, added the new Weston Studio for learning and activities, and a curved glass wall in the shape of Hogarth's Line of Beauty. Delightful re-landscaped and reinterpreted walled garden containing famous ancient mulberry tree.
address: Hogarth Lane, Great West Road, W4 2QN

name: Holy Cross Church, Cromer Street
description: Grade ll listed Oxford Movement Anglican church built 1887-88. Historic England describe the exterior as ‘quirky and aggressive’ but the  interior is ‘very spare and elegant'. The building is  interesting for its 2019 conversion of a crypt area, partly rented commercially to a drama school but also used for community groups. On Historic England's Heritage at Risk register with serious cracks.

name: Holy Sepulchre, Holborn
description: Holy Sepulchre is the City of London’s largest parish Church, also known as the National Musicians’ Church and home to the Musicians’ Memorial Chapel and The Royal Fusiliers Memorial Chapel. St Sepulchre has a long and rich history, with a worshipping community here since at least 1137, a medieval shell and tower that survived the great fire of London and a classical interior.

name: Hopkins Architects
description: The practice's main campus includes two office buildings constructed using its own Patera pre-fabricated system, and linked by a glass reception area and covered walkway.

name: Howard Hodgkin Studio
description: Sir Howard Hodgkin (1932 – 2017) was one of England’s most celebrated contemporary artists. Abstracted yet allusive, apparently spontaneous but in fact highly controlled, his paintings convey feeling through gesture and colour.  His former studio, converted from a nineteenth-century dairy, sits in the heart of Bloomsbury.
address: The Howard Hodgkin Studio, Address tbc to ticket holders, WC1 1AB

name: Ibraaz
description: Ibraaz is a London-based cultural institution for art,  culture and ideas from the Global Majority. Bringing together artists, thinkers, and communities through exhibitions, film, debate, publishing, and multidisciplinary programming, Ibraaz creates a brave space where culture fosters exchange, pluralism, and shared humanity.

name: Inner Space Meditation Centre, Covent Garden
description: Inner Space, London’s oasis of calm, welcomes visitors back for the Open House Festival. Join us over two weekends for free Guided Meditations, Personal Development talks and inspiring wellbeing workshops that support and nurture mindfulness, resilience and inner balance. Take a moment to pause in our Quiet Room, a space that will leave you feeling reconnected, refreshed, uplifted, and renewed.

name: Islington New River walking tour
description: This walking tour will follow the course one of the earliest public infrastructure projects in London, the 400 year old New River aqueduct. Explore a history of innovative public housing developments in one of the most densely populated parts of London and end at New River Head, a striking example of public utility architecture now being repurposed for arts and culture.
address: Outside Canonbury Overground Station, Wallace Road, N1 2PG

name: Isokon Building (Lawn Road Flats)
description: Grade I listed 1934 residential block of flats in Hampstead, designed by the Canadian modernist architect Wells Coates for clients Jack and Molly Pritchard. English Heritage blue plaque for Bauhaus masters Gropius, Breuer and Moholy-Nagy. Museum on site.

name: Jacksons Lane Arts Centre
description: Jacksons Lane’s year-round programme of contemporary performance, arts participation and cultural education exists to empower, and ignite creativity within diverse communities & work tirelessly to overcome traditional barriers through art.

name: Jubilee Hall Parsonage Lane
description: A rare example of a once ubiquitous structure - the military hut. This one probably dates from World War I; it was later sold off and moved to its present site, where it was in turn a Boys Brigade HQ, a book store and, from 1986, the home of the Enfield Society.

name: Kaymet Factory
description: The operational factory of Kaymet, a maker of trays and trolleys since 1947. A hidden 1950s building with a small yard, originally a printing works. It is brick built, with clear-storey glazing and tubular truss north-light main shed roof.

name: Kenwood
description: A striking Neoclassical villa in tranquil gardens on Hampstead Heath, Kenwood boasts breath-taking interiors by Robert Adam and a world-class art collection.

name: King's College London: Museum of Life Sciences
description: This rarely opened space began in 1902 as Guy's Hospital Medical School Library. In 2009 part of it  became the Museum of Life Sciences which houses some rare specimens and part of an historic dental teaching collection..  The building is red brick  with additional stonework and is partially covered in creeper. Internally are original carved oak cabinets and ornate columns.
address: Hodgkin Building, Great Maze Pond, SE1 1UL

name: Kirkaldy's Testing Works
description: Proudly carved over the door are the words ‘Facts not Opinions’. Inside, the authentic sight - and smell - of Kirkaldy’s Testing and Experimenting Works is a unique and direct link with an ingenious age of engineering.

name: Lakeside Centre: Open Art Studios
description: Iconic brutalist building in the heart of Thamesmead, renovation led by Bow Arts Trust in partnership with Peabody, supported by the Mayor’s London Regeneration Fund (LEAP). The centre has opened as a cultural hub for Thamesmead.
address: Southmere Lake Complex, 2 Bazalgette Way (formerly Belvedere Road)

name: Lansbury Lawrence Primary School
description: Lansbury Lawrence (formally Susan Lawrence and Elizabeth Lansbury) opened in the 1951 Festival of Britain as a showpiece of the Live Architecture exhibition in the Lansbury Estate. An interesting mid-century design with original features.

name: Leadenhall Market
description: Iconic Victorian covered market, with roots in Roman Londinium. Today, more than 40 renowned retail brands and outstanding food and drink venues are set within the stunning market place.

name: Leathersellers' Hall
description: New Livery Hall behind a retained early 20th century façade. This is the seventh Hall in the Leathersellers' Company's history since its foundation in the Middle Ages, and is located on the site of its second Hall.

name: Lewisham Arthouse
description: Lewisham Arthouse (LAH) is a not-for-profit artist-led co-operative, based in the formerly Deptford Central Library, Grade II listed, 1910 -1914, Designed by A. Brumwell Thomas (1868 -1948)

name: Life and debt in Southwark
description: Step inside Bankside with Golden Key Academy tour guide Carole Wright  — where prison grounds became peaceful parks and Victorian philanthropists reinvented social housing. Hear about local nurses who fearlessly fought fascism in Spain. Pay respects at a burial ground for women of the night, uncover centuries of queer history hidden in plain sight, and celebrate three hundred years of West African creativity woven into the soul of this remarkable riverside neighbourhood. A walk exploring the working class, global majority and queer history of London's Bankside and Southbank – recounting known and unknown histories next door to the City Wall.
address: John Harvard Library, St Dunstans House, 211 Borough High St, SE1 1JA

name: Lillington Gardens Estate
description: Lillington Gardens in Pimlico, Westminster, was built from 1961 to 1971 by Darbourne & Darke. It set a new standard in high-density public housing with medium-rise structures and private gardens. Blending well with nearby Victorian surroundings, the modernist design won multiple awards and was praised by Nikolaus Pevsner as 'the most interesting recent housing in inner London'.

name: Lloyd's of London
description: Lloyd’s may be the global market for specialist insurance and reinsurance, but it is also a London icon. Over the last three centuries, Lloyd’s has called home to just eight buildings – the most recent of which can be found on Lime Street, in the heart of the City. Designed by renowned British architect Lord Richard Rogers and opened by Her Majesty The Queen in 1986, the Lloyd’s building is a radical addition to the skyline, and a pioneering example of high-tech architecture.

name: London Aquatics Centre
description: The London 2012 Olympic swimming and diving pool. Two  50m pools, 25m dive pool, Team GB dive squad training area.
address: London Aquatics Centre, Queen Elizabeth Olympic Park, Stratford

name: London Open Form Pavilion of Air
description: A floating acoustic architecture, playfully reframing public space as an essential community engagement through sound & site mapping. Accessed by smartphone, headphones & echoes.xyz app, the Pavilion is located outside the Serpentine Gallery,. Drawing on Oskar & Zofia Hansen’s Open Form architectural concept it is one of 15 in a series including Venice, Berlin, Dublin, Bergen and Arctic Norway.

name: London's Roman Amphitheatre
description: The capital’s only Roman Amphitheatre. Regular combined guided tours of Amphitheatre and Guildhall Art Gallery at 12.15pm & 1.15pm on Tuesday-Sunday. Additional Open House tours on 19 and 20 September, please see Guildhall Art Gallery listing.
address: London’s Roman Amphitheatre at Guildhall Art Gallery, Guildhall Yard

name: Lost Aldwych
description: Join SAVE and Dr Tom Bolton on a walking tour of Aldwych. Behind the wide formal streets of Aldwych and Kingsway lies a very different neighbourhood. Clare Market and Drury Lane were a tangle of disreputable alleys until the new streets cut them in half. But traces remain, and this walk dives into the back streets to track the vanished lanes and recreate their past at the core of ancient London.
address: Temple Underground Station, Temple Place, Temple, WC2R 2PH

name: MEplace Nursery Islington
description: A cosy North London nursery, drawing on proven specifications and a collaborative design process.

name: Making public spaces and making spaces public
description: On the borderlands of the City of London, this walk explores how authority and ownership shape our public spaces. It traces the hidden boundaries between different types of public space, asking who gets to make the rules, who benefits, and what the answer tells us about power, property, and public life in the city we share.
address: London Troops War Memorial, Bank Junction, 1 Cornhill, EC3V 3LN

name: Marx Memorial Library & Workers' School
description: Grade II listed, built as a Welsh Charity School in 1738. A library with a focus on Marxism and Socialism since 1933. Lenin worked here 1902-03 and his office is preserved. Fresco by Jack Hastings in 1st floor. Late 15C tunnels.

name: Memorial Community Church
description: Formerly known as Memorial Baptist Church this Grade II listed building opened in 1922, it retains many original features. Open House will include access to the church, gallery and bell tower, and information on church history. 18th September at 7pm Lydia Thornley will lead a talk on the craft skills used in the building, and on the 19th 3.30-6pm there is a sketching workshop

name: Migration tales: Local heroes in Hornsey and Crouch End
description: This walking tour tells the story of how migrants and local heroes played a vital part in creating the fabric of Hornsey and Crouch End. It will explore local communities, people, places, sounds, smells, tastes, textures, and of course buildings and spaces; while telling the story of how the area went from a small cluster of buildings to the multi-cultural neighbourhood it is today.
address: Cafe Merro - 85 Crouch End Hill, N8 8DD

name: Morden Extension Centenary: Tours
description: This year, we are celebrating the centenary of the Morden Extension, designed by Charles Holden. The seven stations of this extension on the Northern line represent both an engineering and an architectural  achievement for London Underground.  This tour will take participants through the stations, describing their architectural details and what it takes to operate them today.
address: Clapham Common Station, The Pavement, SW4 7AJ

name: Morris+Company | ‘The Circular City Starts With Community’
description: Morris+Company is an award-winning architecture practice based in Hackney, east London. We have applied circular economy principles to the retrofit of our own studio, gallery and café space on Mare Street, reducing waste, reusing materials, and designing for longevity.  Through our public exhibition and event programme we place the creative ‘act’ of architecture onto the high street.

name: Museum of Croydon
description:
Explore the Museum of Croydon and Croydon Archives:

- Join the Curator of the Museum of Croydon and the Borough Archivist of the Croydon Archives on an intimate guided tour of our stored, rarely seen collections.
- Explore our current exhibitions with our expert staff, including Grayson Perry's Essex House Tapestries and a brand-new exhibition on Croydon's Architecture

name: Museum of London Docklands
description: Grade I listed, late Georgian sugar warehouse now housing the Museum of London Docklands. Sensitively restored, the new multimedia displays coexist with the massive timber and brick structures of the original building.
address: No. 1 Warehouse, West India Quay (off Hertsmere Road), E14 4AL

name: Museum of the Order of St John
description: St John's Gate and the Priory Church are the remaining buildings from the medieval priory of the Knights Hospitaller and are both Grade I listed. St John’s Gate dates from 1504 and features stunning Victorian and Edwardian interiors. The Priory Church was reconstructed by Seely & Paget after the Second World War, but its 11th-century crypt survives.
address: St John's Gate, St John's Lane, Clerkenwell, EC1M 4DA

name: Muswell Hill Baptist Church
description: A notable example of George Baines' work from the heyday of London free church buildings. It combines Baptist simplicity with Edwardian decor and spaciousness and is broadly unaltered.  It was built to complement the surrounding townscape.
address: Muswell Hill Baptist Church, Dukes Avenue, N10 2PT

name: Mycenae House and Gardens
description: Mycenae House is a former convent run by the Little Sisters of Assumption but is now a community venue with a rich history and story. This tour, talk and exhibition will articulate the buildings life as a convent, as a place of worship and dedication and as a community venue

name: Myddelton House Gardens
description: Visit the lifelong home of Edward Augustus Bowles, one of the 20th century's great gardeners, that was restored with a Heritage Lottery Fund grant in 2011 to tell the story of the famous botanist’s life and gardening style.
address: Myddelton House Gardens, Bulls Cross, Enfield, EN2 9HG

name: National Audit Office
description: A Grade II listed building that is home to the NAO, the UK’s independent public spending watchdog. We support Parliament in holding government to account and help improve public services. First opened in 1939 by Imperial Airways, subsequently BOAC and then British Airways, as an airport terminal. The NAO acquired the building in 1984, with the official opening in November 1986 - 40 years ago!

name: Old Admiralty Building (OAB)
description: Westminster’s grand Old Admiralty Building is the backdrop to many of the UK’s most important ceremonial events. Within its walls some of the most significant – and classified – events in the 20th-century history have happened including the idea behind Operation Mincemeat. Have a chance to look inside a part of this fantastic Grade II Listed Building including the Government Art Collection.

name: Olden Community Garden
description: Olden Community Garden - a hidden 2.5 acre green oasis along a railway embankment in Islington. Sit beside the lawn; listen to birdsong; follow trails through the woodland, meadow and orchard; discover vegetable patches and a wildlife pond.

name: One Paved Court
description: One Paved Court is an artist-run space on a lane of early Georgian shops and houses.  In 2017, Allies and Morrison transformed an old carpet shop into a distinctive home for resident artists and a gallery with an innovative and varied programme of exhibitions. "New interventions are as few as possible, we were there to repair the fabric and to nudge it into its new role." Allies and Morrison

name: Ongéan
description:
Ongéan Ecosystem : 
Art Studios, Gallery, Performance Space, Edible Garden & Kitchen. All built and designed with 99% Reclaimed Materials by artist Adam Ge-Saelis.
address: Ongéan, Park Mews, Croxted Rd, SE24 9DB

name: Open House Festival Hub @ The London Centre
description: Home of NLA, London’s built environment community, and located in the West Wing of the Guildhall complex, the Centre highlights scale architectural models of London: the New London Model and the City Model, in addition to a rotating exhibition highlighting key NLA projects. For 2026, the London Centre will be home to the Open House Festival hub, with a programme of bite-size talks and printed material from the Open City back catalogue available to take home for free.

name: Open Textile Studio and Weaving Exhibition
description: Feathers Place was originally East Lane, connecting Greenwich Park to the river. No 14 has housed the Roan School for Boys, founded in 1643 and more recently contained textile archives of the National Maritime Museum. Today it is Meantime Studios, named after the Prime Meridian of the World on which it sits.  Freeweaver Studio occupies the top floor, a bright vaulted spacious room with skylights.

name: Our Lady of the Assumption Church
description: Grade II* listed building designed by Edward Goldie, built in 1911 in the Gothic style with five buttressed bays. Church interior is simple consisting of large nave and high & deep chancel. Nave side walls show shallow-arched recesses into which are fitted finely carved oak confessional boxes and colourful altars and statues throughout. One of only two Assumptionist Parishes in the UK.
address: Victoria Park Square, Bethnal Green, E2 9PB

name: Our Yard at Clitterhouse Farm
description: Come and visit this grassroots community enterprise where old meets new in the form of the historic farm buildings alongside our crowdfunded cafe. Find out how some of these historic buildings have been saved and lovingly bought back into community use, and find out about our future plans.
address: Clitterhouse Playing Fields, Claremont Rd, NW2 1AP

name: Paekakariki Press
description: Paekakariki Press Ltd is a letterpress workshop containing equipment that can support the letterpress printing processes from casting type to binding a finished book printed on our Heidelberg Cylinder

name: Parish Church of St Andrew, Enfield
description: Grade ll Listed church, that has been much added to over the 800 years of its existence. We have  recently refurbished the organ which has a fine circa 1750s wooden organ case.  The Church has an eight-bell peal still in weekly use– the oldest bell dates from 1680.
address: The Market Place, Church Street, Enfield, EN2 6LL

name: Parish Church of St Mary The Virgin Lewisham
description:
The church was rebuilt in late 15th century with some of that work still remaining to this day.							
During the Festival there will be opportunities to self-guide or to join a group tour which will include access to restricted areas such as the crypt and tower. These last about 30 min and will start on each hour with the last starting at 3 pm

name: Paxton Locher House
description: A unique modern courtyard house making brilliant use of an off-street site on Clerkenwell Green. A retractable glass roof gives wonderful natural light all year round and opens the house to the sky in dry weather.

name: Peace Gardens in London
description: Cycle Tour of Peace Gardens and Open House Properties

name: Peckham in the Balance: Heritage and Activism
description: Come join local architects and activists from Peckham Heritage, Peckham Vision and Peckham Society on a walk exploring Peckham's tangible and intangible heritage. Despite a backdrop of insensitive development proposals, decades of tireless community work continue to shape the area. Come explore with us one of London's most critical questions: 'What does it take to build or to destroy a community?'
address: Peckham Arch, 89 Peckham High St, SE15 5RS

name: People's Museum Somers Town
description:
A great little museum set in the Grade 2 listed Ossulston Estate - a prime example of pre-war Social housing - based on Karl Marz Hof in Vienna.
Open Tuesday to Saturday 10am-5pm, plus Sunday 13th 12am-4pm.

name: Phoenix Gardens Community Building
description: The first purpose-built new-build community centre to be built in the heart of Soho for generations, located within the renowned Phoenix Gardens. Winner: RIBA London Award. Designed by RIBA London Architect of the Year Winner.

name: Piccadilly Rocks!
description: A guided walk looking at the building materials that built a city.  The 90 minute tour around Piccadilly looks at the various rocks that have been used to face the buildings.  The tour uncovers the history and geology behind the key building materials of London.  The tour is lead by Dr Stephen King, a qualified Westminster tour guide and geologist.
address: Outside Royal Astronomical Society, Burlington House, Lond, W1J 0BQ

name: Pimlico Library
description: The story of Pimlico Library reflects the wider history of the neighbourhood, demonstrating how community buildings can adapt and evolve while remaining at the heart of local life.  It is unusual in that it shares the Pimlico Academy Campus with Westminster's Adult Education Service.

name: Pimlico People
description: To celebrate the first ever Pimlico Open House Neighbourhood Festival, cave transforms its gallery space into a virtual map of Pimlico through it's exhibition, The Fabric of Pimlico. Celebrating the actors, authors and musicians who have made it their home over the year....no passport needed
address: Cave Gallery and Studios, 81 Tachbrook Street, SW1V 2QP

name: Pitzhanger Manor & Gallery
description: Designed by Sir John Soane as a family home and country residence. Following a three-year conservation project,  Pitzhanger has been returned to Soane’s innovative original design and re-opened to the public in March 2019.

name: Plaistow Hub
description: Centred on a new public square outside Plaistow Station, Plaistow Hub brings together homes, a library, community facilities and everyday amenities to create a vibrant new destination for local people. The project strengthens connections across the neighbourhood, transforming the station into a welcoming civic heart for Plaistow.

name: Quaker Meeting House - Brentford & Isleworth
description: Come explore a unique example of early Quaker and Georgian architecture. Built in 1785, our Grade II* listed Meeting House is surrounded by quiet and natural grounds, in unbroken use since its founding. Expanded since with new rooms & accessibility features, we invite visitors to enjoy our space, roam in our gardens and take part in a variety of activities and displays by local creatives.

name: Queer Britain
description: Queer Britain Museum is the UK’s national LGBTQ+ museum.    Housed in a converted Victorian building in the heart of the regenerated King’s Cross area, the galleries feature over 200 objects from over 100 years of queer history.   At Open House 2026, Queer Britain’s volunteer guides will give talks demonstrating the museum’s mission to reclaim, preserve and inspire LGBTQ+ history.

name: Quentin Blake Centre for Illustration - New River Head
description:
An industrial heritage site that was the hub of one of London’s first major pieces of urban infrastructure.
Its 18th and 19th century buildings have been restored by Tim Ronalds Architects to create the Quentin Blake Centre for Illustration which opened to the public on June 5th 2026.
address: Quentin Blake Centre for Illustration, Rear of 28 Amwell Street

name: RC Church of St Mellitus
description: A grand neo-classical building of 1871 with impressive interior, built as New Court Congregational Chapel. Home to a Hunter pipe organ, installed as a WW1 memorial and recently restored with National Lottery Heritage Fund support.
address: St Mellitus RC Church, Tollington Park, N4 3AG

name: Rainham Parish Church of St Helen and St Giles
description: Grade I listed Norman church with notable chancel arch with chevron and nailhead ornament, built by Richard De Lucy.

name: Rampayne Street Community Hub
description: Formerly home to the Pimlico Library, the building was transformed into a vibrant, friendly and welcoming community hub.
address: Rampayne Street Community Hub, Rampayne Street, SW1V 2PU

name: Ravensbourne University London
description:
Ravensbourne is a dynamic institution at the intersection of creativity, business, and technology. Based in the heart of North Greenwich, we are home to a diverse, global community.
We learn with industry; industry learns with us. Together we transform lives. With our facilities and strong industry connections, we empower students with the skills, experience and connections needed to thrive.

name: Regent Street Cinema (The University of Westminster)
description: The University of Westminster was one of the first polytechnics in the UK – established in 1838, to educate the working people of London, regardless of background and financial status. Housed in the building is the Regent Street Cinema, widely regarded as the ‘birthplace of British cinema’, with the first public premiere of film in the UK by the Lumière Brothers using the Cinématographe in 1896.

name: Regent's Park Estate Story Trail  Guided Tour
description:
Launched on 24th April 2025, Regent’s Park Estate Story Trail is an exciting new resident-led socially engaged public art trail through Regent’s Park Estate, Euston. 

The trail encompasses 12 site-specific art installations created by 10 artists and collectives, bringing 31 new public artworks to Regent's Park Estate.
address: Old Diorama Arts Centre, 201 Drummond Street, NW1 3FE

name: Revolution, Reform and Regeneration: Somers Town Tours
description: Camden Tour Guides Association will celebrate the history and heritage of Somers Town with a day of dedicated tours exploring the rich social history and architecture of this community, now a regeneration area, sandwiched between the major transport hubs of Euston and St Pancras stations. Hear about its historical roots as a 19th Century slum and the housing reformers who transformed it.
address: Francis Crick Institute, 1 Midland Road, NW1 1AT

name: Romanian Cultural Institute
description: Situated in one of the largest and grandest 19th century squares in London, 1 Belgrave Square was acquired by Romania in 1936 and is now home to the Romanian Cultural Institute.

name: Royal College of Nursing
description: A cleverly integrated mixture of architectural styles and periods, incorporating a late 1720s house (later home to Herbert Henry Asquith) and the purpose-built College of Nursing (1926). Access to main building via guided tour only.

name: Royal College of Pharmacy Museum
description:
Join us for a free guided tour of the RCPharm Museum and Library and find out what crocodiles have to do with pharmacy!
Over 180 years old, the RCPharm Museum and Library is a hidden gem in East London, full of the weird and wonderful world of pharmacy history.
Find out how best to use bear’s grease and explore a collection of poisons even Agatha Christie would swoon at!

name: Royal College of Physicians
description:
Striking, provocative and one of London’s few Grade I listed post-war buildings – welcome to architect Denys Lasdun’s award-winning design. We invite you to drop in, take an expert tour, explore our archives and museum, get creative and more to discover the Royal College of Physicians' London home. 

See https://history.rcp.ac.uk/event/open-house-festival-2026 for more.
address: 11 St Andrew's Place, Regent's Park, NW1 4LE

name: Royal Courts of Justice
description: Architect G.E Street's iconic masterpiece set in the heart of London and one of Victorian England's great public buildings. 13th Century Gothic style given a Victorian interpretation. Commissioned by Queen Victoria in 1870 's to build the home for Civil Justice for the United Kingdom. The cathedral-like Magnificent Great Hall leads off to Historic Oak Panelled Courtrooms.

name: Royal Small Arms Factory
description: Grade II listed arms factory closed to public for 170 years. Museum and clocktower open for tours.
address: RSA Island Centre, 49 Island Centre Way

name: Sacred Grounds / St Anne's Church and Garden
description: Start your exploration of the Open House Soho Neighbourhood with a shot of coffee, a refreshing cold drink and a bite to eat.  Explore our timeline of Soho, and our existing display on the church's history.   Relax in our calm and welcoming gardens.

name: Sacred Heart High School, 212 Hammersmith Road, W6 7DG
description: This historic Grade II* site is shielded from view by a long wall but once inside your eyes and mind will be opened to its extraordinary heritage features such as the cloister garden and 130m of wall paintings, and the hidden history of those who shaped this place from 1669.  Royalty, subterfuge, escape, resistance and an audacious plan.  National Lottery Heritage grant has just been awarded.
address: Sacred Heart High School, 212 Hammersmith Road, W6 7DG

name: Sands End Arts & Community Centre
description: Amongst the RIBA Stirling Prize shortlist 2022 sits Mæ Architect's Sands End Arts & Community Centre in Fulham. The centre consists of a single-storey building comprising bright, airy and flexible event spaces and a community café.

name: Shoreditch Town Hall
description: Join a Guided Tour and explore Shoreditch Town Hall. Opened in 1866 the Town Hall is a Grade II listed, landmark building, and was for over 100 years one of the grandest Vestry Halls in London. Today, we are a leading cultural, community and live events space made up of 70 individual rooms - from the Victorian grandeur of the Assembly Hall to the intimate warren of the untouched basement space
address: Shoreditch Town Hall, 380 Old Street, EC1V 9LT

name: Shrewsbury House
description: Built in 1923, to replace its 18C namesake, Grade ll listed Shrewsbury House is the focus of the Shrewsbury Park Estate conservation area, built 1934-1936 by John Laing and Sons. Two 20th Century Civil Defence buildings are situated within the grounds as well as listed garden features including a recently restored summer house.

name: Sir John Soane's Museum
description:
The extraordinary home of architect Sir John Soane (1753-1837). 

https://www.soane.org/whats-on

name: Sitopia Farm
description: Sitopia Farm is a 2-acre organic and regenerative farm in the London Borough of Greenwich. We are on a mission to improve our food system. We grow vegetables and flowers and sell direct to our local community, to chefs, and to florists. Through our farming and events, courses and community volunteering, we reconnect people to the soil, the joy of good food and flowers, and to each other.

name: Slavery and the City
description: We will explore sites and institutions with direct links to the history of slavery and hear why the apologies were made in 2020, whilst wandering within the story packed streets and alleyways of the Square Mile.

name: Society for the Protection of Ancient Buildings (SPAB)
description: A rare opportunity to explore the Georgian headquarters of the Society for the Protection of Ancient Buildings (SPAB), the UK’s oldest building conservation charity, not normally open to the public.

name: Soho Photography Quarter
description: Architecture studio Klaud leads a tour of the Soho Photography Quarter and The Photographers’ Gallery’s refurbished ground floor, redesigned to connect with this new public space, which features a 45m ‘Artfrieze’ at the heart of a curated public art programme. They are joined by Clare Grafik, Head of Exhibitions at The Photographers’ Gallery, who will present this year’s public space commission.

name: Southbank Printmakers
description:
We are a friendly artist run gallery in Wells Street offering affordable, handmade fine art prints with a broad range of subjects created using many different printmaking techniques.
We aim to encourage people who have never encountered art before to experience printmaking through our regular workshops.

name: Southlands Arts Centre
description: Explore Southlands Arts Centre and discover the history and architecture of this Grade II listed Queen Anne-style building. Admire its distinctive red-brick façade, elegant decorative detailing and historic interiors, and learn how this former private residence has evolved into a thriving community arts centre, celebrating Hillingdon's rich architectural and cultural heritage.
address: Southlands Arts Centre, 75, The Green, West Drayton, UB7 7PW

name: St Alban the Martyr, South Norwood
description: Since 1891, St Alban's has served South Norwood and Thornton Heath; areas that began to develop with the coming of the railways. The church  was  built by the community and is  still serving the community.  The building design altered considerably from start to finish and a small exhibition will give examples of the various suggestions.

name: St Aldhelm's Church, Edmonton - an overlooked gem
description: St Aldhelm's is a Grade-2 listed church designed by the Arts and Crafts-influenced architect W. D. Caröe. Worth visiting for its architecture, it also holds a set of art and stained glass by Walter P. Starmer, famous for his murals at St. Jude-on-the-Hill, Hampstead Garden Suburb. Visitors will be able to see the beautiful cantilevered stone spiral staircase, not usually accessible to the public.
address: St Aldhelm's Church, Silver Street, N18 1PL

name: St Alphege Church, Edmonton
description: The Church of St Alphege is Grade II listed, combining modernist Scandinavian and traditional ecclesiastical forms with good-quality sculptural enrichment; graceful, lofty interiors, with subtle detailing applied consistently throughout.
address: Rossdale Drive/Hertford Road, Lower Edmonton, N9 7LG

name: St Andrew's Kingsbury (new church)
description: Meticulous 1930s rebuilding (complete with original furnishings) of an 1840s Marylebone church. Grade I listed. Contains works by Pugin, Burges, Street, Pearson and Butterfield.
address: Junction of Church Lane/Tudor Gardens/ Old Church Lane, Kingsbury

name: St Anne's Church, Kew Green
description: St Anne's Church, Kew Green was consecrated in 1714. Built with the support of Queen Anne it has been a place of worship for the Royal Families over the centuries. The original 'chapel' has been extended many times and the church is now a little known gem in South West London with a fascinating past.

name: St Anne's Church, Limehouse
description: St Anne's Limehouse has been described as 'the finest parish church in England.' Designed by Nicholas Hawksmoor, it is Grade I listed and one of the Major Churches in the Church of England. It is home to a thriving Christian congregation.

name: St Augustine's Church
description: St. Augustine's, Kilburn affectionately known as 'The Cathedral of North London' was established in 1870. Fr. Kirkpatrick, the first Vicar, engaged John Loughborough Pearson as the architect with the result being what many consider one of his finest works. Externally in 1890 with the tower and spire it became the 2nd tallest building in London (now ecclesiastically 2nd to St. Paul's Cathedral).

name: St Bonifatius RC German Church
description: Centre of German religious and cultural life for more than 200 years. Impressive 20th century church building with contributions from various German artists. Exhibition of German émigré artist Hans Feibusch "Five Stories from the Old Testament" (courtesy of Ben Uri Gallery). Demonstration of the organ by resident organist Paul Dichtl.

name: St Bride's Church, Fleet Street
description: Wren designed building of 1675, interior lost in blitz of 1940, reopened 1957 with 'Wren inspired' interior
address: St Bride's Church, St Bride's Avenue, EC4Y 8AU

name: St George's Cathedral
description: A stunning cathedral in the heart of London. Discover the story of a forgotten masterpiece. Designed by Augustus Pugin and opened in 1848, the original cathedral was hailed as England's foremost Catholic church before an incendiary bomb devastated the building in 1941. Explore the history, architecture and legacy that shaped the Cathedral you see today—and discover its remarkable story.

name: St Giles Parish Church, Camberwell
description:
A large Grade II* listed parish church - built in 1844 it was one of the first churches designed by George Gilbert Scott (St Pancras Station), grandfather of Giles Gilbert Scott (Tate Modern). The church replaced an older medieval church which burned down. 

Key features include the magnificent east window by Ruskin and a Wesley designed organ that is most famous as the origin of ORGANOKE.

name: St James the Less Church
description: One of London's best Victorian churches and a key building in the history of the Gothic Revival. Polychromatic brickwork, with interior art work by G.F. Watts and Thomas Earp, and stained glass windows and painted ceiling by Clayton and Bell. The building is Grade I listed.
address: Thorndike Street,, off Moreton Street, SW1V 2PS

name: St John the Evangelist, Upper Norwood
description: St John's is a Grade II* listed church, designed by John Loughborough Pearson

name: St Lawrence Jewry
description:
First built in c.1136, St. Lawrence Jewry was destroyed in the Great Fire of 1666. The present church was designed by Sir Christopher Wren in 1671. The interiors were destroyed in December 1940 during the World War Two and restored in 1957, faithful to Wren’s original design. Extensive conservation works were completed in 2023.
The official church to the City of London Corporation.

name: St Margaret Pattens Guild Church
description: Take a guided tour of a beautiful example of a Wren church with unique features

name: St Margaret's Parish  Church Barking
description: The parish church of St. Margaret of Antioch Virgin and Martyr is a Grade I listed building dating back to 1215. The church is the living continuation of Barking Abbey, sharing a joint history for centuries.
address: St Margaret's Parish Church, The Broadway, North St, Barking

name: St Mark's Church, Biggin Hill
description:
The Moving Church.
On his appointment to Biggin Hill in 1951, Rev Vivian Symons had the vision to bring the materials for a new church building from the disused All Saints, North Peckham. But first, he had to deconstruct a huge Victorian church, and bring it by himself to its new site.
However, St Mark's is Grade 2 listed, not because of its origin, but due to its style.
address: St Mark's Church, 10 Church Road, Biggin Hill, TN16 3LB

name: St Marks Schoolhouse
