description: Dow Jones Architects has recently refurbished this 1866 listed schoolhouse as their architecture studio. The project has created a light-filled contemporary work space, and demonstrates a sensitive, low carbon approach to restoring a listed building. Artist Richard Castor Jeffery (www.rcjfineart.co.uk) will be showing some of his paintings of buildings and spaces.
address: St Marks Schoolhouse, Battersea Rise, SW11 1EJ

name: St Martin-in-the-Fields
description: One of Britain's finest churches, built in the Italian Baroque tradition and beautifully restored in 2008. Sustainable features include new heating and management systems and lightwell. RIBA Award Winner 2009. Civic Trust Award Winner 2010.

name: St Mary & St Joseph Roman Catholic Church, Poplar
description: Grade II Listed.   Designed by Adrian Gilbert Scott.  Cruciform shape (120 feet by 120 feet) of steel girder and brick construction. Its Lantern tower – based on Ely Cathedral – is supported on parabolic arches 35 feet wide and 50 feet high.  The Stained Glass Windows were designed by John Wilson of Edinburgh and the Stations of the Cross  carved in Blue Horton Stone by Peter Watts.
address: St Mary & St Joseph Church, Upper North Street, Poplar, London

name: St Mary Aldermary
description: The church was first mentioned c1080 and is the oldest of the City churches dedicated to St Mary. It became a Guild Church by virtue of the  City of London (Guild Churches) Act, 1952.  It is the only Wren church built in the Late Gothic style after the Great Fire of London, 1666, thanks to a bequest.

name: St Mary Magdalene
description: An historic living parish church, progressively shaped from the Tudor to the Edwardian period. St Mary's has recently undergone a major refurbishment and the newly restored windows recapture the original airiness of the C18 nave.

name: St Mary Magdalene Church
description: Fine Victorian Gothic church with impressive windows and painted chancel. Paintings by Buckeridge and Westlake 1897. Restoration of chancel paintings was to celebrate the Diamond Jubilee of Queen Elizabeth II (2012).

name: St Mary Magdalene Church & Nature Reserve
description: Grade I listed 12C church, with London's largest churchyard and one of the best-preserved Norman archways in the country, as well as other interesting features, including an anchorite's cell and 750-year-old wall paintings.
address: St Mary Magdalene Church, High Street South, E6 3PG

name: St Mary the Virgin Primrose Hill
description: St Mary's is a Victorian church famous for its second vicar Percy Dearmer who together with Ralph Vaughn Williams produced the English Hymnal in 1906.  We have a rich history of Church Music, beautiful worship and  vestments.  We also have a passion for  social justice within our community.  We were the first parish in Edmonton Diocese to have a woman vicar.
address: St Mary's Primrose Hill, Elsworthy Road, NW3 3DJ

name: St Mary's Church Harrow on the Hill
description: Guided walk (1 hour): On the theme of "everyday histories". We will uncover how ordinary people shaped the landmarks in our area. We look at how St Mary's Church, Harrow on the Hill, drew attention  for over 1200 years, how the core buildings of Harrow School evolved under different architects and how different workforces contributed to the railways and development of Metroland.
address: St Mary's Church Harrow on the Hill, Church Hill,, Harrow, HA1 3HL

name: St Mary's Church, Battersea
description: During Open House, the Friends of Battersea Parish Church present a Floral Festival, organ recitals, historical displays, alongside 3 talks exploring history, creativity, sanctuary & Battersea’s radical past. Sat 12 Sept Dr. Peter Rumley at 6pm, Tues 15 Guy Stagg at 6.30pm,  Thurs 17 at 6.30pm Rory Walsh & Mike Squires.  Plus Join us for Choral Evensong amidst the flowers at St Mary’s Battersea.

name: St Michael and All Angels Church
description: James Maltby Bignall (1827-1885) worked in the practice of Sir George Gilbert Scott, the architect of St Pancras Station. The style of St Michael's is late Gothic Revival, in its size and height reminiscent of Northern European churches.

name: St Olave Hart Street
description: A Great Fire Survivor, damaged in the blitz, the post war restoration of this fascinating building began 75 years ago this year.  Described by John Betjeman as a 'country church in the world of Seething Lane' the building uniquely blends medieval fabric with Festival of Britain era motifs. Explore the medieval crypt, 'Pepys' vestry, church tower and ringing room. Bellringing demonstrations.

name: St Pancras Church & Crypt
description: The church (1822 - Grade I listed) is an early and important example of Greek Revival architecture in London. Significant features include the caryatids and tower copied from models in Athens, and the atmospheric crypt.
address: Euston Road/Upper Woburn Place NW1, NW1 2BA

name: St Pancras Old Church
description: Dating from 11/12C and standing on the oldest site of Christian worship in London (3C). Inside is much 17C ornamentation and outstanding 6C Altar Stone, reputed to have belonged to St Augustine. Surrounding Churchyard, containing tombs of Sir John Soane, Mary Wollstonecraft and others, has been extensively restored and recently refurbished.

name: St Patrick's Church
description: Built thanks to a generous gift from local benefactress, Mrs Lavinia Keene, St Patrick's was consecrated in July 1940 and is unusual in style. The concrete and brick interior contrasts with the dramatic, colourful reredos. Grade II listed.

name: St Paul's Bow Common
description: Described as 'the most significant church built after the WWII in Britain' - Brutalist, inclusive and influential signpost for future church design.
address: Corner of Burdett Road/ St Paul's Way, E3 4AR

name: St Paul's Church, Winchmore Hill
description: Church of England parish church built in 1826-27 by John Davies. It is one of the early Commissioners' churches built after the Battle of Waterloo. It forms part of the Winchmore Hill Conservation Area. The chancel was added in 1888-89, and further extended for the church's centenary in 1928. The church is open daily, and there will be guided tours and a special exhibition 19-20 September.
address: St Paul's Church, Church Hill, N21 1JA

name: St Paul's, Newington
description: Modern architecture church with large copper and lead roof and concrete, brick and stained glass external structure. Marble, wood and plaster interior and artwork by Sculptor Freda Pinto and Gerald Holtom.

name: St Peter’s Church
description: This Victorian flint faced church is a Commissioner's or Waterloo Church designed by Sir George Gilbert Scott and consecrated in 1851. Set in a closed churchyard with areas for wildlife there is a striking grave to a major benefactor. The east window was made by Whitefriars. There is a self guided tour and videos including a wedding peal on our ring of 12 bells. Refreshments are available.
address: St Peter’s Church, St Peter’s Road, Croydon, CR0 1HG

name: St Vedast alias Foster
description: 12C church. During the Great Fire of 1666 the church building escaped total destruction, and was restored. Christopher Wren was eventually called in to rebuild St Vedast, completing the work in October 1673.

name: St. George Villa
description:
Tranquility in an urban environment, this project has transformed an unloved basement into a light filled, sustainable, calming home.

A deep retrofit using low-carbon materials, including a high level of insulation, a natural swimming pool, rainwater harvesting and a green roof, this home explores how we can transform high density urban areas into places of harmony between people and nature.

name: Stalls and Shops: a walking tour of Lewisham Market
description: Join the Stall Tales local history team for a walking tour of Lewisham's market and high street. Discover the hidden history of the market, which began in the 1890s with a few unlicensed stalls, and spent decades fighting for legal recognition. We will look at the market as a temporary architecture, local retail landmarks, and reflect on the changing face of shopping in the high street.
address: Lewisham High Street (Shopping Centre Entrance Canopy), SE13 7HB

name: Star Wars Tour of London
description:
An unofficial walking tour of London film locations used in Star Wars. Learn about the crucial role the city played for three different empires, Roman, British, and Galactic! 

Discover how London's Barbican Estate was the perfect shooting location for a dystopian view of the science fiction city of Coruscant. 

Learn how London and the destiny of Star Wars are so deeply intertwined!

name: Station Lodge
description: A unique new build residence with an impressive triple-height living space under a roof with a fully exposed steel and timber structure and an inbuilt design with a potential to be easily split into two separate houses in the future

name: Straw-ctural Designers
description: Scale Rule brings young people together with architects and structural engineers to design and build their ideal school space, with a focus on interacting with our natural environment. Pick a prompt card - a library in a treehouse, a canteen on the canal, a rooftop forest playground  - then sketch it and build it in straws and paperclips alongside practicing professionals.
address: Canal Building, Regents Wharf, 10–18 All Saints Street, N1 9RL

name: String House - Camberwell
description: Contemporary timber frame home with unique string screen; a postwar house reassembled to follow passive house principles. The structure was built in 7 weeks to create a reimagined flexible home of two halves enabling an Airbnb rental that bypasses the first floor kitchen & living area, located to borrow views towards mature trees at the rear & city buses to the front expanding senses & spaces.

name: Strongroom
description:
Established 1984, Strongroom has produced some of the biggest records in British music and remains the largest independent recording studio in East London. 

Featuring unique visual design by legendary artist Jamie Reid (Sex Pistols), these spaces are unlike any other. Reid's work draws from druidic culture and sacred geometry to convey vital messages of hope, environmentalism and anti-fascism.

name: Swakeleys Estate
description: A most important house in Ickenham, an outstanding example of Jacobean architecture built in the 1630s. Red brick construction laid in English bond on an H plan. Great Hall includes the 1655 Harrington Screen, 18C marble fireplace panelling.
address: Swakeleys Road, Ickenham (access from Milton Road), UB10 8LD

name: Swiss Cottage Library
description: Grade II listed building by a renowned Modernist which has been refurbished and remodelled whilst protecting the building's landmark status.

name: Sydenham Garden
description:
At Sydenham Garden, we promote health and wellbeing, support recovery and build connection with nature, gardening, creative expression, and with each other. We provide therapeutic group activities for people who are referred to us.
 
We're opening our Wynell Rd site on Sat 19th Sept; come & visit our buildings, green spaces, view exhibited artworks and have a slice of cake in the garden.

name: TOMA House + Studio
description: A self-built project by the founder of east London architecture practice TOMA Studio, this mid-terraced Victorian house has been completely re-imagined over the course of three years. The house balances refined detailing with experimentation to create a spacious and comfortable family home, which also accommodates an architecture practice and pottery studio within a Shou Sugi Ban garden room.

name: Temple Bar
description: Temple Bar is a 350 year old gateway to the City of London, designed by Sir Christopher Wren. It formerly stood in Fleet Street, and is the last surviving gateway to the City of London. This beautiful structure has a fascinating history, which will be revealed to visitors.
address: First Floor, Paternoster Lodge, 2 Paternoster Square, EC4M 7DX

name: The Albany
description:
South East London's leading arts centre,.
The Albany is the engine room for people to reach their creative potential, tell their stories and define their own culture. Together we will inspire new possibilities for positive change.  
The Albany is an incubator for new ideas and initiatives. Our Creative Strategy places democratic, community-led approaches at the heart of everything we do,

name: The Annual Sedici Post Grad Group Exhibition
description:
Now in its seventeenth year, Sedici consists of artists from many countries who are now based across England. Working across eclectic mediums and subject matter, this diverse body of artists shares an independent and contemporary purpose highlighting the ongoing strength of Art being made today. 

The gallery itself is a reimagined, mid-century school gymnasium with original details

name: The Annunciation Marble Arch
description: The Annunciation is a dramatic Gothic Revival building tucked behind the Marble Arch end of Oxford Street. The Grade II* church was built by Sir Walter Tapper in 1912-1914.

name: The Arches
description: The Arches invites you to explore its artists' work in a newly designed framework by A347, focused on fostering community-minded practices. With spaces centered around a communal core, the open layout encourages collaboration and interaction. Meet the artists, experience their work firsthand, and purchase directly from them, making artistic creation a tool for community building.

name: The Barbican & The City Gardens
description: The Barbican is a residential complex of around 2,000 flats, maisonettes, and houses in the City of London. Built on the site destroyed by The Blitz during the World War II, The Barbican Estate is a fascinating development and an icon of Brutalist architecture. Architects were Chamberlain, Powell and Bon. You will find an oasis in the middle of buildings, with gardens and water features.

name: The Battle of Britain Bunker - The Generator House
description: Explore the Generator House at RAF Uxbridge’s Battle of Britain Bunker. Normally off‑limits to the public, it houses the original 1930s standby generator that powered the underground Operations Room coordinating RAF Fighter Command in WWII. It offers a glimpse into wartime engineering, featuring preserved machinery, original fittings, and fascinating stories.  Free admission, no booking required.

name: The Brunel Museum
description: London's story of an engineering family that changed the world. Dramatic new staircase below sculpture garden leads to underground chamber. Travel by train through first underwater shopping arcade & fairground to view Thames Tunnel portico.

name: The Butcher, The Baker and The Candlestick Maker
description: Trade and craft guilds have flourished for centuries. The City of London’s Livery Companies are unique in their survival, number, and diversity. While the original social and economic conditions that created these original guilds have long been overtaken by modern commerce, these fascinating institutions still flourish today. Join us to explore their enduring history and modern impact.

name: The Caravan Gallery comes to Croydon: Surrey Street
description: The Caravan Gallery is a unique documentary photography project and exhibition focused on Croydon's built environment. The Caravan Gallery photograph the sur/reality of everyday life and work with communities to explore people's connection to place, exhibiting their photographs of the area in a small caravan.

name: The Catford House
description: The Catford House is a newly refurbished pub and community kitchen run by GCDA. The oldest surviving building in Catford was revitalised by Hayatsu Architects as part of Lewisham Council’s town centre regeneration. Led by architect Takeshi Hayatsu, the Open House tour explores the building’s repair, exposed structure and adaptation for community use.
address: The Catford House, Catford Broadway, SE6 4SP

name: The Clockworks
description: The Clockworks is the only museum in the world dedicated to electrical horology. A major collection of clocks and timekeepers charts the development of networked and precision timekeeping, from 1840-1970, while an onsite workshop showcases modern and heritage clock conservation in action.

name: The Crafted Environment: Merton Abbey Mills
description: Studio AVC is an architecture and interior design practice based in the historic 1929 Shop at Merton Abbey Mills—Join us for a short talk on William Morris and how the Arts & Crafts movement continues to inspire our designs today. Afterwards, we’ll take you on a guided tour of Merton Abbey Mills, the historic heart of Arts & Crafts making.
address: Unit 11, The 1929 Shop, Merton Abbey Mills Mills    London SW19 2RD

name: The Evolution of Eye Care: Museum Tour
description: The museum houses hundreds of artefacts that provide a rich history of the instruments, innovations and patient care over the last 300 years. There are glass cabinets that display some of the artefacts.  Much of this collection and its display has been built up by Richard Keeler, who is a widely published expert on ophthalmic history. He has been the Honorary Museum Curator since 1999.
address: The Royal College of Ophthalmologists, 18 Stephenson Way, NW1 2HD

name: The Great Fire of London
description:
On Sunday, 2 September 1666, the Great Fire of London started at a bakery in Pudding Lane, destroying thousands of homes, 87 churches, and St. Paul's Cathedral.
On this walk, we will explore this dramatic story, discover the causes and outcomes of the fire and see how Christopher Wren helped rebuild the city from the ashes.

name: The Hospital Chapel of St Mary & St Thomas
description: Founded c1145 by the Abbess of Barking as a hospice for thirteen old and infirm men, the present building is 12C and 19C. Grade II* listed with many interesting monuments, including Burne-Jones windows.

name: The John Morden Centre and Morden College Almshouses
description: Morden College is a charity founded in 1695 by Sir John Morden. For over 330 years, it has provided safe, high quality homes that support independence, dignity and belonging later in life. Join a guided tour of its beautiful buildings, from the historic grade I listed Quadrangle to the award winning John Morden Centre, winner of the RIBA Stirling Prize.
address: Morden College, 19 St Germans Place, SE3 0PW

name: The King's Foundation - Charlotte Road
description: A refurbished factory warehouse, the repurposed space now hosts educational programmes and activities of the School of Traditional Arts and the architectural team of the King’s Foundation. Live demonstrations of traditional arts skills by students and alumni, scheduled talks on KF's architectural projects, and guided tours all await the visitor.

name: The Lansbury Estate: Festival of Britain, Poplar 2026
description: Guided tours exploring The Lansbury Estate and it's role in the Festival of Britain, 1951. Discover why 86,000 people travelled on special busses to Poplar to marvel at this new neighbourhood, designed to be a blueprint for Britain's post-war recovery. 45-minute-long walking tours led by knowledgeable local guides.
address: The Hive, 167a East India Dock Road, E14 0EA

name: The Lloyd's Register Building
description: The Lloyd’s Register Building at 71 Fenchurch Street, is the historic headquarters of Lloyd’s Register. Opened in 1901 and designed by Thomas Collcutt, it is a grand classical stone palazzo with rich decorative detailing that reflects the organisation’s status and global ambition. Its architecture combines ornate interiors and artistic craftsmanship with new contemporary workspaces and innovation.

name: The Lock House, Richmond Lock & Weir
description: The Lock House is part of Richmond Lock & Weir, on the left bank of the Thames at Richmond. Originally home to the resident lock keeper, it is now the design studio and exhibition space of Astronaut Kawada, architects and designers. They have fully refurbished the interior of the Lock House to create a series of spaces to complement the remarkable and unique qualities of the main structure.
address: The Lock House, Ranelagh Drive, TW1 1QZ

name: The London Archives
description: The London Archives' older building was built in the late 1930s for the Temple Press and has many original features. Purpose built extension in early 1990s for archival storage. Public rooms remodelled by Bisset Adams in 2000s.

name: The Old Fire Station
description: The Old Fire Station is now a thriving community centre run by the Holloway Neighbourhood Group. It has been redeveloped for this purpose, now housing a community room, garden room and hall. The building has many original features (notably on the outside) and even though the usage has changed dramatically it remains an important emergency service for many in the local area.

name: The Old Fire Station Community Centre N16
description:
•⁠   Find out more about what goes on here 
•⁠   ⁠Informal building tours 
•.  Meet our Old FireStation community
•.  Explore images from our archive
•⁠   Seasonal food and drink ( pay what you can)
•⁠   Music, games, share stories
•⁠  All ages welcome

Discover more about the working history of our landmark community building; it's past present and future and get to see behind the scenes!
address: The Old Firestation, 61 Leswin Road, N16 7NX

name: The Priory and Old Library, Orpington
description: Grade II listed building dating back to 1270. Following the dissolution of Christ Church Priory in Orpington in the 1530s, the house became a rectory. Additions were built in 1959 to put in a library.

name: The Purpose of Light: Exhibition by Misan Harriman
description: The Purpose of Light, Misan Harriman’s landmark photographic exhibition, bears witness to significant  moments, not with judgment or ideology, but with a deep and unflinching empathy for the human condition. Featuring 110 unique photographs, this exhibition is a call not for division, but for togetherness.

name: The Ragged School SE1
description: Built in 1907, The Ragged School SE1 has been part of the community for nearly 120 years.  starting off as a poor school in the worst and first borough of London, the school aimed to transform lives of the ragged children that lined the streets.  The church then took over the school to form a club,  pass through developers into the hands of an artist.  The White room will open for creative delight.
address: The Ragged School, 47 Union Street, SE1 1SG

name: The Royal Society
description: A spectacular Grade I listed building designed by famed architect John Nash. Built in 1831, these former townhouses have undergone refurbishments throughout their history. The building is now home to the UK's national science academy.
address: The Royal Society, 6-9 Carlton House Terrace, SW1Y 5AG

name: The St Michael Steiner School
description: Our school resides in a Grade II listed building on the edge of Hanworth Air Park. Fortescue House was the rectory for St. George's church on the edge of Hanworth Air Park. Later, it became a school, and now it is the home to the St. Michael Steiner School. We are blessed by beautiful grounds & woodland where the children can play & relax.  We enjoy the unique history and biodiversity of the area.
address: The St Michael Steiner School, Park Road, Hanworth, TW13 6PN

name: The Story of Housing in Hackney: A Guided Walking Tour
description: The tour traces changing ideas about housing, community and urban life. Highlights include the Keeling House, Lennox House, Nisbet House and the Chowdhury Walk. Along the way, we will discuss the architects, planners and communities that shaped these buildings, and consider how their social ambitions continue to influence Hackney today.

name: The West End At War
description: A special exhibition exploring the people and places that shaped the area during the Second World War. Tracing famous figures who made Soho their home, and the ordinary everyday heroes who kept the area functioning and our spirits up!

name: Thornhill Square
description: A tour of one of the largest and best preserved early Victorian squares and gardens in London, also with a magnificent and original public library of 1906, which shows Byzantine and Art Nouveau influences, and a remarkable Gothic church. Refreshments available.
address: Main door of St Andrew’s Church, Bridgeman Road, N1 1BQ

name: Tools for Urban Narratives
description: During the festival, Lorenzo Zandri’s studio transforms into an immersive environment that bridges the gap between architectural theory and photographic practice. Eschewing traditional construction to focus on the 'process of the image’, Zandri will present an analytical overview of his practice and research – where photography serves as a tool for urban narrative rather than mere documentation.
address: Bodney Road Studios, 1 Bodney Road, Unit 2, E8 1AY

name: Tooting Bec House
description: A double storey rear extension and refurbishment to a Victorian terraced house in Tooting Bec, South West London

name: Trent Park: House of Secrets
description: Trent Park House of Secrets is a new museum in a historic country house in Enfield, North London, which recently opened to the public. From glittering 1930s social hub to WWII interrogation centre, the stately home witnessed some of the most closely guarded secrets of the 20th century. This extraordinary story of espionage, courage and creative deception has remained largely untold for over 70 yea
address: Trent Park House, Daffodil Crescent, Enfield, EN4 0PS

name: Triangle House
description: Winner of the 2025 Camden Design Award for small projects and the 2024 'Don't Move Improve' award for best project under £100k. A self build 39m2 triangular micro home converted from a former mechanic's garage,  creating a flexible and multifunctional home fit for living and working in.  Come and see sliding beds, triangular sofas and a pocket garden.

name: Trinity Buoy Wharf/Container City
description:
Home to London's only lighthouse, fine stock buildings, examples of the innovative Container City buildings and SS Robin, the world’s only surviving complete
Victorian steamship. This former buoy manufacturing site is now a centre for the creative industries with various sculptures and installations.

name: Tuckey Design Studio
description: This transformation of a derelict pub into an architecture studio doubles up as a gallery and lecture theatre. The new office is an example of the practice’s approach towards existing structures and intelligent architectural interventions.

name: Twickenham Museum
description: Grade II listed former waterman's cottage c1720. Restored and converted into a museum celebrating the rich history of Twickenham, Whitton, Teddington and the Hamptons.

name: UAL School of pre-degree studies at 40 Lime Grove
description: 40 Lime Grove has provided creative education to young people for over a century. Opening in 1908 as the Hammersmith College of Art and Building, it is now UAL School of Pre-Degree Studies. A handsome building, influenced by the Arts and Crafts style with gables, mullioned windows, and steep pitched roofs, it is  listed Grade II by Historic England. There is also a listed Mulberry tree.

name: UNIVERSITY OF WESTMINSTER: NCS and Tower Tavern
description:
The University of Westminster's New Cavendish Street campus, designed by Lyons, Israel and Ellis  represents an important moment in the evolution of the architecture of the modern polytechnic. 
Visitors will explore the campus through guided walks. 
The programme concludes in the University's Tower Tavern, a former public house -  for an evening reception and talk, Pints and the Poly.

name: Union Chapel
description: A Grade I and II*  listed architectural gem that’s home to an inclusive non-conformist church, an award winning venue, a rare and historic pipe organ, Sunday School Hall community hub, and The Margins Project supporting those facing homelessness and pertinent social justice issues.

name: Unit 13
description: Unit 13 is a space of many parts -  office, workshop, venue, exhibition space, and screening room. It is concieved as a social space in which to collaborate. A place of exchange - both ideas, skills, knowledge, and energy. During the working week we have three architecture practices working from the space - AH A, LSD, and TJA - alongside a revolving exhibition. During the weekend, we have talks.

name: University of East London - Architecture and Visual Art
description:
The University of East London’s Architecture and Visual Arts is a lively School that combines, Architecture, Physical Design and the Visual Arts. This perfect combination of creative programmes cross-pollinate, providing a fertile ground for creation, arts and design.
Our presence  will feature guided tours to the state-of-the-art facilities, creative studios, and ‘Way out East’ gallery.

name: Van Gogh House London
description: The carefully renovated Van Gogh House seeks to share its story and inspire a new generation of artists through Van Gogh’s London story. The house curates a dynamic programme of events anchored in the artist’s practice and local heritage.

name: Vyner Studios
description:
Visit Vyner Studios, the new home of Studio Bark and U-Build. This light-touch retrofit turns a stranded warehouse into a circular 'Material Bank.' 

Modular U-Build partitions can be endlessly unbolted, proving interiors are adaptable assets, not sunk costs. Finished with plywood, acoustic Hemspan, cork and clay paints, it offers a radical, healthy blueprint for future creative workspaces.

name: Walking Stories: Haringey Golden Key Academy exhibition
description: Step inside and discover the eight community-led walking tours exploring Haringey’s people, places and histories. Walking Stories: Haringey brings together photographs, maps, archives, artwork and stories from across the borough. The exhibition at Birch Arts CIC gallery, in one of Blue House Yard’s distinctive colourful huts, is created by the Golden Key Academy tour guide course participants.
address: Birch Arts Gallery, Blue House Yard, Wood Green, N22 7TB

name: Walthamstow Pumphouse Museum
description: Grade II listed Victorian engine house remodelled to take a pair of 1895 Marshall steam engines, still in working order. A museum celebrating the rich Industrial Heritage of the Borough and the Lea Valley Region.

name: Wapping Hydraulic Power Station
description: A rare opportunity to see inside Wapping Hydraulic Power Station, built in 1890 and London's last hydraulic power station to be decommissioned. The site has been closed for the last ten years, but is now entering a new era under the custodianship of Glass Castle Foundation, which has begun restoration ahead of plans to breathe new life into the building as a  centre for experimental arts.
address: Wapping Hydraulic Power Station, Wapping Wall, E1W 3SF

name: Warehouse Art Collective
description: In our community, creativity is a way of life. Warehouse residents forge friendships, make art and host events in our unique spaces. A few of us will open the doors of our alternative lifestyle and show what it is like to live and thrive in the warehouses. The public can engage with contemporary art in the live/work industrial units of the Haringey Warehouse District.

name: Water Lane Building - Trigon Fire Safety
description:
We are a fire safety consultancy working in the built environment. We provide fire safety advice to architects, designers, engineers, building owners, building managers etc.
We are based in Richmond and recently completed our own fit-out of the first floor.
address: Water Lane Building, 83-84 George Street, Richmond, TW9 1HE

name: Wennington Parish Church of St Mary and St Peter
description: Grade II listed Norman church dating from as early as 1190 and as late as 1248.

name: West Wickham Library
description: Modern public library extended and reimagined 2023-2025, re-opened 2025 with improved library facilities, makerspace, business lounge, community space, Bromley Historic Collections displays, garden and café. London Borough of  Bromley Regeneration Team project, architects Brimelow McSweeney, library operators GLL.

name: Westminster Quaker Meeting House
description: Three centuries of Quakers in Westminster.  Opened in 1883, with front doors added in the 1920s. It was bomb-damaged in 1941 and rebuilt in 1956. Grade II listed registered place of worship, it contains a peaceful meeting room and 1950s wood panelling and fittings.

name: What makes a good school?
description: We attend primary school at an impressionable age and this is often our first experience of wider society.  The word 'school' is used to mean the social institution and the physical building but neither is fixed - both are subject to change.  This walking tour will explore the evolution of school building design, teaching practice and attitudes to education in Southwark between 1873 and 2022.
address: Jamaica Gate, next to Southwark Park Lodge, Southwark Park, SE16 2ET

name: WilkinsonEyre
description:
WilkinsonEyre has built some of the world’s most recognisable landmarks. Our global portfolio includes the spectacular restoration of London’s Battersea Power Station, Gardens by the Bay in Singapore and buildings for Apple, Facebook and Dyson. 

Explore our new studio in Shoreditch - designed by us - to see where we explore, innovate and create.

name: William Mitchell's Mural at Brooklands Primary School
description: Join us at Brooklands Primary School to discover more about the story of William Mitchell’s mural (1958), designed as part of the London County Council’s pioneering Design Consultant Scheme
address: Brooklands Primary School, Medbourne Close, SE3 9AB

name: Wimbledon Windmill Museum
description: Rare example of a hollow post mill (1817). Grade II* listed, it now contains a museum depicting the history and development of windmills in Britain. Many working models, windmill machinery, equipment and tools.

name: Women of learning and law on the Strand
description: Join us for a walking tour along a short but remarkable stretch of the Strand and Aldwych, where centres of law and learning have flourished from Tudor times to the present day. Along the way, we will hear the stories of the women — and a few men — connected to this corner of London: royal residents, scholars, activists, lawyers, artists and athletes who lived, worked, studied here, and went on to change the world. We will look at the buildings and artworks that carry their traces and walk in the footsteps of some of history's most formidable women, who opened doors for those of us who came after them.

name: Wrotham Park
description: A privately-owned Grade II listed Palladian mansion with grand interiors restored in 1883, set in 300 acres of parkland in the midst of 2,500 acres. Built for Admiral The Hon. John Byng.

name: Zoroastrian Centre For Europe (formerly Grosvenor Cinema)
description: Grade II* listed Art Deco building with well-preserved interior. Auditorium with deep coved ribs; proscenium arch flanked by fluted columns. Restoration fully funded by in house donations from Zoroastrian faith community, without government grants.

name: outhouse gallery
description:
outhouse gallery is a small, independent, artist-run creative space located in Brunswick Park, Camberwell. 
As a former public toilet, the gallery's mission is to be open, public and accessible to both facilitators and visitors - from free exhibitions, live performances, and workshops to publishing articles online and in outhouse magazine.
